title: Data graphs: pie charts and line graphs
subject: math

doNow.prompt: Two line graphs show sales rising. Graph A looks much steeper than graph B, but graph A has an axis of 0 to 50 and graph B has an axis of 0 to 200, and both sales rose by 20. Which graph had the bigger increase?

choices.text: Graph A, because its line is steeper
choices.misconception: A steeper line always means a bigger increase.

rationale.chose: The learner selected option Graph A, because its line is steeper as their answer to this question.
rationale.thinks: They are applying the coded wrong turn instead of checking the axis scale before comparing how steep two lines look.
rationale.reteach: Reteach from the paired notes trap: A steeper line always means a bigger increase.. Steepness is judged by the drawing rather than the axis scale behind it. Slope depends on the axis scale: two graphs can have the same rise but look different. In the animation scene s4 both shops rose by +20, from 20 to 40, even though one line looks steeper.
